_meta.description: Prompt templates for synthetic consumer generation
_meta.notes: Based on the approach described in Maier et al. The system prompt primes the LLM as a consumer with demographic attributes in a survey setting. The elicitation prompt asks for free-text purchase intent.

system_prompt.template: You are participating in a consumer research survey. You are a {age}-year-old {gender} living in the {region} of the United States{income_clause}{ethnicity_clause}. Reply briefly to any questions posed to you.

variable_definitions.income_clause: Optional. Appended as: ' with a {income_level} household income'. Values: low | moderate | upper-moderate | high. Omit if unknown.
variable_definitions.ethnicity_clause: Optional. Appended as: ' who identifies as {ethnicity}'. Omit if unknown — paper found ethnicity poorly replicated.

examples.full_demographics: You are participating in a consumer research survey. You are a 34-year-old woman living in the Midwest of the United States with a moderate household income. Reply briefly to any questions posed to you.
examples.minimal_demographics: You are participating in a consumer research survey. You are a 52-year-old man living in the South of the United States. Reply briefly to any questions posed to you.
examples.no_demographics: You are participating in a consumer research survey. Reply briefly to any questions posed to you.

design_notes: Keep the system prompt short and factual. Do not add personality traits or consumption habits — let the LLM infer those from demographics.

The paper found that prompting WITHOUT demographics still produced good distributional similarity (KS=0.91) but poor correlation attainment (rho=50%). Demographics are essential for ranking concepts correctly.
'Reply briefly' is important — it prevents the LLM from generating essay-length responses that embed multiple conflicting sentiments.

image_stimulus.description: Preferred method. Send the product concept as an image (the concept slide containing description and optional mockup art). Attach as an image in the user message.

text_stimulus.description: Fallback when images aren't available or supported. Transcribe the concept description as plain text.
text_stimulus.notes: Paper found image stimulus slightly outperformed text-only in most experiments. Use image when possible.

purchase_intent.question: How likely would you be to purchase this product?
purchase_intent.notes: This is the core question. Do not constrain the response format — let the LLM respond freely in natural language. Do not ask for a number.

reasoning_followup.question: What specifically about this product makes you feel that way? What would make you more or less likely to buy it?
reasoning_followup.notes: Stage 2 follow-up. Asked after the initial purchase intent response. Uses the same persona and concept context. Response is stored separately and never touches the SSR scoring pipeline. Provides qualitative insight into drivers and barriers.

concept_relevance.question: How relevant is this concept for you?
concept_relevance.notes: Paper tested this as a secondary question. Requires its own reference sets (not the purchase intent sets). Achieved rho=82% SSR, rho=91% FLR with Gem-2f.

prompt_assembly_order: 1. Set system prompt with persona demographics
2. Send concept as user message (image preferred, text fallback)
3. Send elicitation question as follow-up user message
4. Collect free-text response (Stage 1 — used for SSR scoring)
5. (Optional) Repeat elicitation for n=2 samples per persona for stability
6. Send reasoning follow-up question (Stage 2 — qualitative only, not scored)
7. Collect reasoning response (stored separately, never embedded or scored)
